title: NavigationHistoryEntry.url censoring uses the wrong referrer policy

labels.name: topic: navigation API
labels.description: The navigation API: navigation, NavigateEvent and intercepted navigations

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

**Title:** `NavigationHistoryEntry.url` censoring uses the wrong referrer policy

### Summary

The [`url` getter](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-navigationhistoryentry-url) returns null when the entry's [document state](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#she-document-state)'s [request referrer policy](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#document-state-request-referrer-policy) is "`no-referrer`" or "`origin`". The WPTs for this feature expect a different policy: the referrer policy of the entry's own document, including changes a `<meta name="referrer">` makes while the document is active.

### What the spec says

Step 4 of the `url` getter:

> If *she*'s document does not equal *document*, and *she*'s document state's request referrer policy is "`no-referrer`" or "`origin`", then return null.

The request referrer policy is the policy used to fetch the document. [navigate](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#navigate) step 24.4 sets it from the *referrerPolicy* argument, which comes from the `referrerpolicy` attribute on the `<a>`, `<area>` or `<iframe>` that started the navigation. It defaults to the empty string, and nothing changes it after that. The note under [document state](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#document-state-2) makes the distinction itself:

> The request referrer policy is distinct from the history policy container's referrer policy. The former is used for fetches *of* this document, whereas the latter controls fetches *by* this document.

So the spec only censors an entry when the navigation that created it asked for no-referrer. A document that sets its own policy, through a `Referrer-Policy` header or a `<meta name="referrer">`, has no effect.

### What the tests expect

All three tests in `navigation-api/navigation-history-entry/` set the policy on the document itself and never use a `referrerpolicy` attribute:

- `no-referrer-url-censored.html`: the iframe document is served with `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.
- `no-referrer-from-meta-url-censored.html`: the iframe document contains `<meta name="referrer" content="no-referrer">`.
- `no-referrer-dynamic-url-censored.html`: the test inserts `<meta name="referrer" content="no-referrer">` after the document has loaded, navigates away, and expects `entries()[0].url` and `activation.from.url` to be null. It then goes back, replaces the meta with `same-origin`, navigates forward, and expects the URL to be visible again.

In every case the iframe is fetched with the default request referrer policy, so the spec algorithm as written returns the URL and all three tests should fail.
